_readme: Built by scripts/build-guides.mjs from data/guides.json. One ready-made Facebook post per guide step.

posts.title: Set your budget and get preapproved
posts.socialPost:
Thinking about buying on the Mississippi Gulf Coast? Step one is a preapproval, and a monthly budget that includes taxes, insurance and flood coverage, not just the mortgage. On the Coast, insurance can swing the payment a lot from one house to the next.

Buyer guide, step 1: https://bill-temple-realtor.vercel.app/guides/buying.html#budget

posts.title: Price insurance early
posts.socialPost:
Gulf Coast buyers: get flood and wind insurance quotes on the actual address before you make an offer. Look up the flood zone on FEMA's map, and ask about the hurricane deductible. It's often a percentage of the home's value, not a flat amount.

Buyer guide, step 2: https://bill-temple-realtor.vercel.app/guides/buying.html#insurance

posts.title: Choose your agent
posts.socialPost:
Buying a home? Before you tour with an agent, you'll sign a written buyer agreement that explains what they'll do for you and how they're paid. Agent pay isn't set by law and is negotiable. Ask questions until it makes sense.

Buyer guide, step 3: https://bill-temple-realtor.vercel.app/guides/buying.html#agent

posts.title: Find the right town and home
posts.socialPost:
House hunting on the Gulf Coast? Look beyond the house: check the flood zone, ask for an elevation certificate, and see how the lot drains. Two similar homes a few blocks apart can have very different insurance costs.

Buyer guide, step 4: https://bill-temple-realtor.vercel.app/guides/buying.html#search

posts.title: Make an offer
posts.socialPost:
Making an offer on a Mississippi home? Read the seller's Property Condition Disclosure Statement closely. It covers flood zones, past flooding, flood insurance premiums and water or storm damage. It's what the seller knows, so still get your own inspection.

Buyer guide, step 5: https://bill-temple-realtor.vercel.app/guides/buying.html#offer

posts.title: Inspect the home
posts.socialPost:
Under contract on a Gulf Coast home? Use your inspection days for a full home inspection, a termite inspection, and firm insurance quotes. Ask the inspector about roof age, past water damage and drainage, the same things insurers ask about.

Buyer guide, step 6: https://bill-temple-realtor.vercel.app/guides/buying.html#inspect

posts.title: Finish the loan, appraisal and insurance
posts.socialPost:
Closing on a Coast home? Your lender needs proof of homeowners insurance, and flood insurance if the home is in a high-risk zone. Ask whether the seller's flood policy can be transferred to you. It can sometimes keep the current pricing.

Buyer guide, step 7: https://bill-temple-realtor.vercel.app/guides/buying.html#loan

posts.title: Close and get your keys
posts.socialPost:
About to close on a home? Never wire money based on an email alone. Call your closing attorney or title company at a number you already know is real to confirm the instructions. Real closing offices don't change wiring instructions by email.

Buyer guide, step 8: https://bill-temple-realtor.vercel.app/guides/buying.html#close

posts.title: After you move in
posts.socialPost:
Bought a home in Mississippi this year? If it's your main home, file for homestead exemption at your county Tax Assessor's office between January 1 and April 1. It lowers your property taxes, and missing the deadline means waiting another year.

Buyer guide, step 9: https://bill-temple-realtor.vercel.app/guides/buying.html#after

posts.title: Find out what your home is worth
posts.socialPost:
Thinking about selling on the Mississippi Gulf Coast? Start with what your home would really sell for, based on recent sales near you, and an estimated net sheet that shows what you'd walk away with after payoff and costs.

Seller guide, step 1: https://bill-temple-realtor.vercel.app/guides/selling.html#value

posts.title: Gather your paperwork
posts.socialPost:
Selling on the Gulf Coast? Get your paperwork ready before you list: elevation certificate, flood policy and premium, roof age and any FORTIFIED certificate, termite bond, and repair receipts. Buyers and their insurers will ask.

Seller guide, step 2: https://bill-temple-realtor.vercel.app/guides/selling.html#paperwork

posts.title: Fill out the seller's disclosure
posts.socialPost:
Selling a home in Mississippi? Most sellers must give buyers a Property Condition Disclosure Statement covering the roof, water damage, past flooding and flood zone. Fill it out honestly before you list. If it's late, the buyer gets a few days to walk away.

Seller guide, step 3: https://bill-temple-realtor.vercel.app/guides/selling.html#disclosure

posts.title: Get the house ready
posts.socialPost:
Getting ready to sell? Fix what an inspector or insurer will flag first, like roof leaks, signs of water and old systems. Then declutter, clean and tidy the yard. Big cosmetic projects rarely pay back as much as people hope.

Seller guide, step 4: https://bill-temple-realtor.vercel.app/guides/selling.html#prep

posts.title: Price it and go live
posts.socialPost:
Listing your home? Price it right from day one. Homes get the most attention in their first couple of weeks. Ask your agent to show you the comparable sales behind the price, and make sure the photos and video do the house justice.

Seller guide, step 5: https://bill-temple-realtor.vercel.app/guides/selling.html#list

posts.title: Compare offers
posts.socialPost:
Got more than one offer on your home? Compare the whole package: price, financing, earnest money, inspection timeline, closing date and any requests for credits. The highest number isn't always the one that closes.

Seller guide, step 6: https://bill-temple-realtor.vercel.app/guides/selling.html#offers

posts.title: Work through inspections
posts.socialPost:
Under contract as a seller? After inspections, the buyer may ask for repairs, a credit or a lower price. You can agree, counter or decline. Having your roof paperwork and elevation certificate ready can keep the deal moving.

Seller guide, step 7: https://bill-temple-realtor.vercel.app/guides/selling.html#inspection

posts.title: Close the sale
posts.socialPost:
Selling your home? Keep your homeowners and flood insurance in force until the sale actually closes. If the buyer is taking over your flood policy, the closing office can help with the transfer.

Seller guide, step 8: https://bill-temple-realtor.vercel.app/guides/selling.html#close

posts.title: After the sale
posts.socialPost:
Just sold your home? Save your closing statement and improvement receipts, and talk to a tax professional about the federal home-sale exclusion. Many sellers of a main home can exclude some or all of the gain if they meet the rules.

Seller guide, step 9: https://bill-temple-realtor.vercel.app/guides/selling.html#after
